description: The Master of Advanced Studies in Climate Science and Policy (MAS-CSP) is a one-year professional degree that gives students the knowledge they need to become leaders in the field of climate policy. Offered by Scripps Institution of Oceanography, the MAS-CSP curriculum is designed to teach students the fundamentals of climate science, how to evaluate the impacts of climate change, and how to effectively communicate and implement solutions. The program combines coursework from the physical, biological, and social sciences with professional training in communication and policy-making. Graduates of the MAS-CSP program are prepared to pursue careers in a wide array of fields, including government agencies, non-profits, and the private sector.
Program name: Master of Advanced Studies in Climate Science and Policy

description: The Master of Science degree in Earth Sciences is a graduate program offered by the Earth Science program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, in conjunction with the Graduate Division at UC San Diego. The program is designed for students who are interested in a terminal master’s degree with a focus in a specific area of Earth Sciences. The Earth Sciences M.S. degree provides a strong foundation for a variety of career pathways in industry, government, and education, and gives students the tools necessary to tackle a wide range of environmental problems. M.S. students will engage in a rigorous curriculum that includes quantitative coursework and training in computational analysis. The program also requires the completion of a capstone project which can be either a research-based thesis or a literature-based review paper on a topic of the student’s choosing, conducted under the supervision of a faculty advisor. The curriculum is intended to be completed in one year, but can be extended to two years for students with limited prior training in Earth Sciences.
Program name: Master of Science in Earth Sciences

description: The Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans, and Planets (GEO) curricular group at Scripps Institution of Oceanography encompasses a broad range of scientific disciplines focused on the Earth’s physical, chemical, and biological systems, from the deep interior to the oceans and atmosphere. Researchers in GEO study the fundamental processes that govern the evolution of the planet, the causes and consequences of natural hazards like earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, and the dynamics of the Earth’s climate system. The GEO curricular group emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach, combining field observations, laboratory experiments, and computational modeling to address some of the most pressing scientific questions of our time. Students in the GEO curricular group have the opportunity to work with leading experts in their fields, and to conduct research in some of the most remote and challenging environments on Earth. The GEO curricular group is also home to a number of world-class research facilities, including the Cecil H. and Ida M. Green Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP), the Geosciences Research Division (GRD), and a number of analytical laboratories.
Program name: PhD in Earth Sciences

description: The Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) Program is an optional specialization in the PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. PIER is designed to train a new generation of scientists and leaders to research and solve complex and interdisciplinary environmental problems. The PIER program provides an opportunity for students to specialize in a chosen field of research and to acquire the breadth and skills to work on problems that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries. Students gain this experience through a combination of interdisciplinary courses, seminars and colloquia, and an internship program that places them in a non-academic environment to gain experience in applying their knowledge. Admission to the PIER specialization is a two-step process. First, students must apply and be admitted to the PhD program at Scripps. Once accepted into the Scripps PhD program, students may apply to the PIER program for admission.
Program name: PhD in Earth Sciences with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research

description: The Joint Doctoral Program in Geophysics with San Diego State University (SDSU) is a PhD program that operates under the framework of the existing Scripps Institution of Oceanography PhD program. Students have access to the broad resources of both institutions. In addition to a rigorous training in the fundamentals of geophysics, the program exposes students to a variety of research topics, and provides flexibility in designing a course of study that best suits their interests. Students interested in the Joint Program in Geophysics can apply through either UC San Diego or SDSU. Admission requirements are the same for both institutions and applications are evaluated by a joint admissions committee. Applicants are encouraged to contact potential advisors in their area of interest at either or both institutions.
Program name: PhD in Geophysics (Joint with San Diego State University)

description: The Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) degree in Marine Biodiversity and Conservation (MBC) at Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego is a 12-month, intensive program that is geared towards resource managers, environmental consultants, and informal science educators. Our goal is to train the next generation of leaders in marine conservation. This is accomplished through a comprehensive curriculum of interdisciplinary coursework and a collaborative, solution-based capstone project. In just one year, our students receive a broad introduction to the science, economics, and policy of marine conservation and gain practical skills to improve their effectiveness in the environmental arena.
Program name: Master of Advanced Studies in Marine Biodiversity and Conservation

description: The master of science (M.S.) in marine biology is a two-year course of study that provides a broad, interdisciplinary education in marine biology. The M.S. degree is earned by the satisfactory completion of a minimum of 36 units of graduate coursework and the successful completion of a capstone requirement. The M.S. is considered a terminal degree at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, and students admitted to the M.S. program will not be able to transfer to the Ph.D. program. The marine biology M.S. degree is a Plan II (non-thesis) degree. The capstone requirement will consist of either: 1) a literature-based capstone paper and its defense at an oral examination, or 2) passing the Ph.D. departmental exam. Both options require an extensive literature review that demonstrates mastery of a specific area of marine biology. The capstone project must be completed by the end of the student’s second year of study.
Program name: Master of Science in Marine Biology

description: The Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in marine biology science. Research in the Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps is managed through three multi-disciplinary research sections: Integrative Oceanography Division (IOD), Marine Biology Research Division (MBRD), and Center for Marine Biotechnology and Biomedicine (CMBB). Students are admitted into the PhD program and receive their degree through the Scripps Oceanography department. Marine Biology students are part of a unique department that houses a large diversity of scientific disciplines that all have in common a focus on the oceans. This allows for a truly interdisciplinary educational experience for our students. In addition to a broad suite of graduate courses in marine biology, students have access to courses in the other curricular programs at Scripps (Climate-Ocean-Atmosphere; Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans, and Planets; Ocean Biosciences) and in other departments at UC San Diego (e.g., Division of Biological Sciences, School of Medicine, Skaggs School of Pharmacy).
Program name: PhD in Marine Biology

description: The Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in marine biology and biological oceanography. Students are encouraged to develop their own research program from a wide range of fields including ecology, physiology, molecular biology, and symbiosis, applied to a diverse array of ocean ecosystems and organisms, ranging from microbes to whales. Marine Biology PhD students are based in two research sections at Scripps, Marine Biology Research Division (MBRD) and Integrative Oceanography Division (IOD). The core of the PhD curriculum is an interdisciplinary education in ocean sciences along with in-depth knowledge in marine biology and biological oceanography, and professional training in science communication, grant writing, teaching, and leadership. Students also have the option of pursuing a PhD specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research. This specialization is for students interested in an interdisciplinary approach to research on environmental problems. Graduate students affiliated with PIER gain a broader perspective and a specialized skillset to tackle the world’s most challenging environmental problems.
Program name: PhD in Marine Biology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research

description: The Master of Science in Oceanography at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is a terminal Master’s degree intended for students who have a strong science background and wish to get interdisciplinary training in oceanography. This degree provides students with knowledge of the diverse sub-disciplines of oceanography and the tools to succeed in a variety of related careers in industry, government, or education. The program takes between one to two years to complete. Students are required to take 36 units and complete a capstone project. Students work with a faculty advisor and a capstone committee to design and complete their project.
Program name: Master of Science in Oceanography

Concentration name: Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans and Planets (GEO)
description: The PhD in Oceanography degree program is an advanced, research-based degree that requires the completion of a dissertation of publishable quality that makes an original and significant contribution to oceanography. The program is organized into three separate Curricular Groups: Climate-Ocean-Atmosphere Program (COAP), Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans and Planets (GEO), and Ocean Biosciences Program (OBP). Students enroll in one of the three Curricular Groups based upon their research interests.
Program name: PhD in Oceanography

description: The Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) PhD specialization is designed to allow students to pursue interdisciplinary environmental research and to provide them with the background necessary to be leaders in the field of environmental research. Students admitted to the PIER specialization pursue research and coursework that is truly interdisciplinary, spanning the natural and social sciences. Students are expected to define and pursue a program of study and research that includes two or more of the traditional disciplines. Students in the PIER specialization are expected to fulfill all of the curricular requirements of their home PhD program plus PIER-specific requirements.
Program name: PhD in Oceanography with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research

Concentration name: Anthropology of the Subject, Person, and the Individual
description: The doctoral program in Anthropology at UC San Diego is one of the top programs in the country. We are ranked 6th in the nation in the most recent National Research Council (NRC) rankings of graduate programs. We are also ranked among the top programs by other measures, such as the number of federal grants received by our graduate students for their dissertation research. The department’s distinguished faculty is one of the most outstanding in the country in terms of its scholarly productivity and its success in training graduate students. We have a distinct profile in American anthropology due to the strong integration of its subfields—archaeological, biological, sociocultural, and linguistic anthropology—and its close ties with other disciplines, interdisciplinary programs and research centers across the campus. We admit a small, select group of students each year. This allows for close intellectual engagement between faculty and students.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology

description: The Department of Anthropology and the interdisciplinary Cognitive Science Program offer an interdisciplinary Ph.D. in Anthropology and Cognitive Science. The program provides a unique course of study for students with interests in both Anthropology and Cognitive Science. Students in the program receive a solid grounding in both fields, and do research that is jointly supervised by faculty from both departments. Students apply through and are admitted into the Anthropology department. For information about the Cognitive Science program and faculty, please visit the Cognitive Science website.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology and Cognitive Science

description: The Anthropological track of the Science Studies Program focuses on the ethnographic study of science, technology, and medicine. Anthropological science studies scholars analyze scientific and technical work where it happens -- in laboratories, clinics, and field sites -- as well as in the social worlds where scientific knowledge and technologies circulate. Anthropologists of science, technology, and medicine pay close attention to the ways in which local and global relations of power shape and are shaped by technoscience. The track brings these ethnographic sensibilities to the interdisciplinary field of science studies. Our faculty's expertise is global in scope, with particular strengths in Latin America, the United States, and Asia. Faculty and graduate students in the track are affiliated with a number of interdisciplinary programs on campus, including the Institute for Practical Ethics, the Center for Global Health, and Critical Gender Studies.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology (Science Studies)

description:
The Anthropology Department, in collaboration with the Center for Academic Research and Training in Anthropogeny (CARTA) and the Salk Institute for Biological studies, offers a PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny. This specialization is designed to train graduate students in the transdisciplinary field of anthropogeny. Anthropogeny investigates the origin of humans. This is a vast and complex topic, requiring the integration of multiple disciplines from the social, behavioral, biomedical, and biological sciences.
The primary goals of this specialization are: To help students develop the ability to communicate across the different disciplines that contribute to anthropogeny. To provide a foundation of knowledge across these disciplines. To foster the transdisciplinary way of thinking that is necessary to fully explore the origin of humans.
Students will: Attend a three-quarter course sequence in anthropogeny. Participate in a quarterly CARTA-sponsored symposia series. Be eligible to receive fellowship support.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny

description:
The Department of Anthropology, in conjunction with the Interdisciplinary PhD Program in Cognitive Science, offers a specialization in cognitive science for students in sociocultural, psychological, or biological anthropology. Anthropology is the study of human beings in the widest possible sense. It is a discipline that is global in its scope, historical in its depth, and holistic in its approach. Cognitive science is the interdisciplinary study of intelligent systems, both natural and artificial. It draws from anthropology, computer science, linguistics, neuroscience, philosophy, and psychology. The specialization in cognitive science is intended to provide anthropology students with a deeper understanding of the theories and methods of this allied discipline and to allow them to pursue research that crosses the boundaries between the two fields.

At the core of the specialization are two year-long proseminar courses that introduce students to the essential concepts and methods of cognitive science and a practicum in which students gain hands-on experience in the laboratory of a cognitive science faculty member. Additional advanced courses are available on a wide variety of topics. Students who complete the specialization will receive a parenthetical on their diploma: “PhD in Anthropology (with a Specialization in Cognitive Science).”
Program name: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Cognitive Science

description: The Department of Anthropology at UC San Diego is committed to the four-field approach, integrating sociocultural anthropology, biological anthropology, psychological anthropology, and anthropological archaeology. We also have a strong focus on the anthropological study of language and communication. The Ph.D. program is designed to provide the theoretical background and methodological skills necessary for a career in professional research and teaching in anthropology. The department has a strong focus on the anthropology of the Americas and the Pacific Rim.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Computational Social Science

description: Our doctoral program in Anthropology offers a rigorous training in the four sub-fields of the discipline: sociocultural, biological, and archaeological anthropology and anthropological linguistics. Although students are admitted to a specific sub-field, they are expected to gain a broad understanding of the whole discipline and to develop a research project of their own that may draw upon more than one sub-field. The first two years are spent in coursework, at the end of which students must pass a foreign language exam and write a second-year paper. After advancing to candidacy, by passing a qualifying exam, students carry out a major piece of independent fieldwork. The final stage of the program is the writing of a doctoral dissertation. While the department offers a focus in each of the four main sub-fields of anthropology, it is well known for a number of specializations that cut across these. These include: psychological anthropology, medical anthropology, the anthropology of modernity, the anthropology of religion, political anthropology, the anthropology of climate change, human-animal-environmental interactions, and the study of language in society.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies

description: The Department of Anthropology at UC San Diego offers a program of graduate studies leading to the PhD degree. The Department has a distinctive profile within the discipline of anthropology. We are well-known as a department that is theoretically innovative and that bridges the traditional sub-fields of the discipline through an interdisciplinary and contemporary focus. We are committed to a comparative and critical understanding of what it is to be human in a complex and changing world. Our graduate curriculum reflects our department’s intellectual profile and commitment to holistic and integrated anthropology for the 21st century. The PhD program offers two specializations: Anthropogeny and Interdisciplinary Environmental Research. The Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research is designed for doctoral students who wish to communicate and collaborate with researchers across a wide range of academic disciplines in the natural sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities that are pursuing environmentally-focused research. The graduate Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research is a PhD specialization that may be taken in conjunction with any of the PhD degree programs at UC San Diego.
Program name: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research

description: The Astrophysics Ph.D. is an interdisciplinary program that includes researchers from the Department of Physics and the Center for Astrophysics and Space Sciences (CASS). CASS is one of the largest and most vibrant astrophysics groups in the world, with a broad range of research interests, including cosmology, galaxy formation, high-energy astrophysics, and exoplanets. Our astrophysics program emphasizes a broad education in fundamental physics as well as a focus on cutting edge research. Students are encouraged to get involved in research during their first year. Research at UC San Diego spans the full range of observational and theoretical astrophysics. We have a diverse faculty that actively participate in student mentorship. UC San Diego is a major partner in the Lick and Keck observatories, which ensures our students and faculty have guaranteed access to world-class facilities. We encourage you to browse our faculty page for more information on the research being carried out at UC San Diego. Our graduate students are also encouraged to interact with the broader San Diego astronomy community through events like the San Diego Astronomy Journal Club (SDAJC). For more information, please visit our prospective students page or attend one of our info sessions.
Program name: PhD in Astronomy and Astrophysics

description: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) is a professional degree that replaced the master’s degree as the entry-level degree for audiologists. The joint Au.D. program between San Diego State University and the University of California, San Diego provides students with a strong scientific and theoretical foundation in hearing and balance sciences and disorders, as well as extensive and varied clinical experiences. The program is designed to train audiologists to be leaders in the field and to provide the highest quality, evidence-based services to their patients. Graduates of our program are employed in a wide variety of clinical settings (e.g., hospitals, private practices, ENT offices), industry, and educational and research settings.
Accreditation status: The Doctoral Program (Au.D.) in Audiology at San Diego State University and University of California, San Diego is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.
Program name: Doctor of Audiology (AuD) (Joint with San Diego State University)

description: The Department of Bioengineering offers a Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Bioengineering. The M.S. program is designed to provide a deeper level of education than is possible in the B.S. program, but not the extensive research and specialization of the doctoral program. For this reason, the M.S. program may be a desirable terminal degree for students who plan to seek industrial employment or it may be a desirable intermediate degree for students who wish to enter the doctoral program at a later date. Both a thesis and a non-thesis option are available for the M.S. program. For both options, all M.S. students must successfully complete a set of core courses. This requirement is intended to provide a broad, graduate-level background in physiology, tissue engineering, and biomechanics. Beyond these core courses, M.S. students are encouraged to specialize by selecting a sequence of courses in their area of interest.
Program name: Master of Science in Bioengineering

description: The Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with the background, training, and original research experience to become successful independent investigators in academia or industry. The focus of the program is on the integration of principles and applications from engineering, biology, and medicine. The Ph.D. program is research-oriented and requires the completion of an independent research project and a dissertation. The program culminates in the Ph.D. in Bioengineering degree. This requires completion of at least 48 units of coursework, research, and seminar, passing a departmental qualifying examination, and defending a dissertation that describes the results of original and independent research.
Program name: PhD in Bioengineering

description: The goal of the MS in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology is to train the next generation of scientists who are able to analyze large-scale biological and clinical data sets and to develop novel computational and mathematical approaches to solve pressing problems in biology and medicine. This MS program provides a rigorous, interdisciplinary training that combines coursework in biology, computer science, mathematics, statistics, and bioinformatics, with a thesis research project that will allow students to gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge research. The program prepares students for positions in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries as well as for entry into Ph.D. programs in bioinformatics and other related fields. The Bioinformatics and Systems Biology (BISB) MS degree program requires a minimum of forty-eight units of coursework, research, and a written thesis. The MS program takes approximately two years to complete, with a maximum time limit of three years.
Program name: Master of Science in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology

description: The Ph.D. in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology is an interdisciplinary program that brings together faculty from the Division of Biological Sciences, the School of Medicine, the Jacobs School of Engineering (Departments of Bioengineering, Computer Science and Engineering), and the Physical Sciences Division (Departments of Chemistry & Biochemistry and Mathematics). The interdisciplinary nature of the program is ideal for students with undergraduate degrees in a wide range of fields, including biology, biochemistry, chemistry, computer science, mathematics, and bioengineering. The program aims to train the next generation of scientists who can bridge the fields of biology, medicine, and computer science and engineering; as such, we offer a rigorous and flexible curriculum that can be tailored to an individual student's interests. The program is committed to a culture of collaboration with students at the very core of our program. Students are mentored by top-tier faculty who are experts in their fields, and have the opportunity to participate in a variety of research areas.
Program name: PhD in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology

description: The M.S. degree is offered in two plans. A terminal M.S. degree (Plan I-Thesis) is available to students who have been admitted to the Ph.D. program and have successfully passed the first year of Ph.D. core classes and their first-year rotation. The Contiguous B.S./M.S. program (Plan II-Comprehensive Exam) is offered as a five-year program for UC San Diego undergraduate students. Both programs are administered by the Biology M.S. Committee.
Program name: Master of Science in Biological Sciences

description: The graduate program in Biological Sciences at UC San Diego is a fast-paced, interactive and high-caliber environment for training young scientists. Our program is interdisciplinary and features research in seven main areas: Cell Biology, Development & Genetics; Ecology, Behavior & Evolution; Molecular Biology; Neurobiology; Plant Biology; Quantitative Biology & Bioinformatics; and Microbiology. The program is built on a foundation of cutting-edge research and a curriculum of challenging and exciting courses that lead to a Ph.D. in Biology. The Ph.D. Program is a full-time, year-round program that trains students for careers as research scientists and educators.
Program name: PhD in Biological Sciences

description: The Master of Science degree program in the Biomedical Sciences is a graduate program offering a Plan I (Thesis) and a Plan II (Comprehensive Examination). The degree may be a terminal degree or obtained in the course of a PhD program. The graduate program also offers a combined BA/MS degree program for undergraduate students at UC San Diego. The program involves didactic courses and an independent research project performed under the supervision of a faculty member. The MS degree requires an oral defense of the thesis or a comprehensive exam. Both plans require a minimum of 36 units.
Program name: Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences

Concentration name: Bioinformatics, Anthropogeny, Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP)
description: The Biomedical Sciences (BMS) PhD Program is an interdisciplinary, interdepartmental graduate program that provides a state-of-the-art PhD training environment that is collaborative and highly interactive. Students will receive training in the classroom and in the laboratory in a wide range of topics that span the continuum from basic to translational “bench to bedside” research. All BMS students are provided with a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of biomedical sciences through both didactic course work and laboratory research. The program offers tracks and specializations that allow students to obtain more in-depth training in specific areas including Bioinformatics, Anthropogeny, and the Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP).
Program name: PhD in Biomedical Sciences

description: The Master of Science in Biostatistics is an exclusively-designed program of the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science that aims to train the next generation of biostatisticians who will have a strong quantitative background, an understanding of the biological mechanisms of disease, and the ability to apply statistical methods to solve problems in public health and biomedical sciences. Our graduate students are provided with rigorous classroom instruction and hands-on data analysis experiences that prepare them for careers in academia, industry, and government. The curriculum is designed to be completed in six quarters, although it is possible for some students to complete the program in less time. For more information regarding our program including course requirements, please visit the UC San Diego Course Catalog and the program's Student Handbook.
Program name: Master of Science in Biostatistics

description: The Ph.D. in Biostatistics is an interdepartmental program offered by the Division of Biostatistics in the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science and the Halicioglu Data Science Institute, in affiliation with the Department of Mathematics. The program is designed to train independent researchers in biostatistical theory and methodology. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in academia, industry and government. The program requires a dissertation. Students in this program will learn to build a strong foundation in statistical theory and methods. They will learn to apply statistical methods to the design of experimental and observational studies in the health sciences and to the analysis of data from such studies. Students will also gain the skills to extend existing statistical methods and to develop new ones for applications in the health sciences. The program emphasizes the important role of computing in modern statistics and ensures that students become proficient with a number of statistical software packages. Finally, through required coursework as well as seminars and research collaborations with faculty, students will learn to effectively communicate the results of their statistical analyses to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Program name: PhD in Biostatistics

description: The UC San Diego Rady School of Management’s Master of Science in Business Analytics (MSBA) is a STEM designated program that will provide you with the required skills to succeed in data-rich business environments. The program offers a rigorous, hands-on training that will prepare you to use data and analytics to identify business opportunities, generate business insights and create business solutions. As an MSBA student, you will gain the quantitative skills to create and manage business analytics and the business acumen to lead data-driven decision making.
Accreditation status: The Rady School of Management at UC San Diego is accredited by AACSB International — The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Program name: Master of Science in Business Analytics

description:
The Master of Finance program at the Rady School of Management at UC San Diego prepares graduates to tackle significant challenges facing the financial industry.

Rady School Master of Finance graduates are empowered to launch careers at investment banks, commercial banks, asset management firms, consulting firms and other private and public sector organizations around the world.

The Master of Finance curriculum will provide you with a solid foundation in econometrics, financial modeling, financial econometrics, data analytics, and empirical finance. You will gain a deep, theoretical understanding of financial markets that will prepare you for a dynamic career.
Accreditation status: The Rady School of Management at the University of California San Diego is accredited by AACSB International — The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB International is the longest-serving global accrediting body for business schools that offer undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral degrees in business and accounting.
Program name: Master of Finance

description: The Rady School’s Master of Professional Accountancy (MPAc) program provides you with the skills necessary to succeed in the field of public accounting. MPAc students learn from the top accounting scholars and practitioners in the world. Our curriculum is data-analytics driven and our graduates are equipped with the skills and knowledge needed to be successful in the ever-changing accounting profession.
Accreditation status: The Rady School of Management at UC San Diego is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Program name: Master of Professional Accountancy
Master of Science in Business Administration

description: The Rady Full-Time MBA program is a STEM Designated program that develops visionary, ethical leaders who make a positive impact in the world through innovation, collaboration and knowledge. You will focus on your career goals from day one, giving you the foundation to become a leader who can identify new ideas, develop them and take them to the marketplace. Our curriculum provides a strong foundation in the core disciplines of business with an emphasis on innovation and data-driven decision making. You will learn from world-class faculty who are renowned experts in their fields and are committed to your success. Our small-by-design class size fosters a close-knit community where you will build lifelong relationships with your classmates and our faculty. Our MBA program is designed to help you develop the skills and knowledge you need to succeed in today's competitive business world. We offer a variety of hands-on learning opportunities, including our signature Lab to Market capstone course sequence, internships and case competitions. You will also have the opportunity to participate in a variety of extracurricular activities, such as student clubs, speaker series and networking events.
Accreditation status: The Rady School of Management at UC San Diego is accredited by AACSB International – The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Program name: Full-Time MBA

description: The Rady FlexMBA program is designed for working professionals who want to push their leadership potential to the next level without pausing their careers. With a curriculum focused on innovation and data-driven decision making, the Rady FlexMBA will equip you with the business acumen and leadership skills to make an immediate impact and transform your career.
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).
Program name: FlexMBA

description: The Rady Executive MBA is a 21-month program focused on innovation and data-driven decision making. It’s for experienced professionals who are ready to rise into leadership positions or grow their own company. Taught by our world-class faculty, the program will equip you with the knowledge you need to advance your career. You’ll become adept at identifying new business opportunities and turning them into successful ventures. Rady’s collaborative culture allows you to learn from your peers’ diverse experiences and build a life-long network of trusted advisors. You will grow through a hands-on approach to learning, with real-world applications of course material.
Accreditation status: The Rady School of Management at UC San Diego is accredited by AACSB International — The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Program name: Executive MBA

Concentration name: Marketing, Finance, Management, Economics and Strategy, Operations and Analytics, Innovation, Technology and Operations, Accounting
description: The Rady School of Management PhD Program is a full-time, five year program focused on producing cutting-edge research. The program prepares students for a career in academia at a top-tier university. Rady PhD students are a select group, admitted to work closely with Rady faculty on research. Students specialize in one of seven areas of study, but are encouraged to pursue interdisciplinary research. Rady faculty members are leaders in their fields with a track record of top-tier publications in marketing, finance, management, economics and operations.
Accreditation status: The Rady School of Management at the University of California San Diego is accredited by AACSB International — The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB International is the longest-serving global accrediting body for business schools that offer undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral degrees in business and accounting.
Program name: PhD in Management

description: The M.A. degree is intended for students who want a broader-based master’s degree. Students who wish to enroll in the M.A. degree program must be admitted to the department’s Ph.D. program. There is no direct admission to the M.A. program. After completion of one year of study in the Ph.D. program, students may petition to change from the Ph.D. program to the M.A. program. The M.A. is a non-thesis degree and requires the completion of 36 units of course work. At least 24 of these units must be in chemistry, and at least 12 of the 24 units must be in graduate-level chemistry lecture courses. The remaining 12 units can be in any graduate-level science, math or engineering courses, or in upper division undergraduate courses in these fields with consent of the vice chair for the graduate education committee. In addition, the student must have a B average in the course work. All M.A. degree requirements must be completed within two years. M.A. candidates are not eligible for any financial support from the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry.
Program name: Master of Arts in Chemistry

description:
The M.S. degree is offered with a major in chemistry. It is not required as a prerequisite for the Ph.D. degree. The M.S. degree in chemistry may be taken with one of three plans:
Plan I (Thesis): A minimum of 36 units of credit is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level courses. The remaining 12 units must be in upper-division (100-level) or graduate-level courses. A maximum of 12 of the 36 required units may be taken for a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory grade. At least 12 of the 36 units must be in chemistry research (CHEM 299). A thesis is required. The thesis must be approved by a committee of three faculty members, and the student must pass an oral examination on the thesis research.
Plan II (Comprehensive Examination): A minimum of 36 units of credit is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level courses. The remaining 12 units must be in upper-division (100-level) or graduate-level courses. A maximum of 8 of the 36 required units may be taken for a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory grade. No more than 4 of these units can be in non-letter graded research, CHEM 297 or CHEM 299. Satisfactory performance on a comprehensive examination is required.
Plan IV (Coursework): A minimum of 48 units of credit in upper-division (100-level) and graduate-level courses is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level chemistry courses, excluding special study (CHEM 296, 297, 299). A maximum of 8 units of upper-division courses may be taken in a related field. No units of research (CHEM 299) may be included in the 48 units of credit. Satisfactory performance on a comprehensive examination is required.
Program name: Master of Science in Chemistry

description: The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry offers a program of graduate study leading to the Doctor of Philosophy. The PhD program is designed to develop students into scientists who are experts in their chosen area of research. These areas include Analytical, Atmospheric, Biochemistry, Biophysics, Chemical Biology, Inorganic, Nanoscience, Organic, Physical, and Theoretical Chemistry. The program provides the broad chemical background required to support this development as well as opportunities for students to develop skills as teachers and mentors.
Program name: PhD in Chemistry

Concentration name: Behavioral Medicine, Experimental Psychopathology, and Neuropsychology
description: The SDSU/UC San Diego Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Clinical Psychology is one of the nation's outstanding clinical psychology doctoral programs. The program has been continuously accredited by the American Psychological Association since 1989. The program's mission is to train clinical psychologists who are well-grounded in the science of psychology and who will be able to apply their scientific knowledge and methods to the advancement of human welfare. The program faculty have a wide range of interests which is reflected in the three major areas of study offered in the program: Behavioral Medicine, Experimental Psychopathology, and Neuropsychology. The program is committed to fostering diversity among its faculty and students.
Accreditation status: The program has been continuously accredited by the American Psychological Association since 1989.
Program name: PhD in Clinical Psychology (Joint with San Diego State University)
Master of Arts in Communication

description: The Department of Communication at UC San Diego offers a doctoral program that is distinctive in its dual focus on communication as a social and a cultural practice, and on the central role of communication and media technologies in shaping and transforming these practices. We are committed to a critical and empirical approach to the study of communication. The program is interdisciplinary in its orientation, drawing on faculty and curricula in the humanities, social sciences and to a lesser extent, in the fine arts and engineering. We offer a single, integrated PhD program in Communication, one in which students must work across at least two of the department’s three main areas of research.
Program name: PhD in Communication

description: The Science Studies Program at UC San Diego is a joint doctoral program of the Departments of Communication, History, Philosophy, and Sociology. It is the oldest and one of the most respected programs of its kind in the world. The program offers interdisciplinary training for students to study the historical and contemporary connections among the sciences, social sciences, humanities, technology, and medicine. Core requirements include a two-quarter Core Seminar and a one-quarter seminar on contemporary science, technology, and medicine studies. Elective seminars from the four participating departments provide the primary course work for students. The Departments of Communication, History, Philosophy, and Sociology each admit students into the Science Studies Program. Applicants should specify which of the four departments they wish to apply to on the university’s application form.
Program name: PhD in Communication (Science Studies)

Concentration name: Programming Languages, Compilers, and Software Engineering
description: The M.S. program is intended to be a terminal professional degree. The curriculum is a mixture of courses and a research project or thesis intended to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for a professional career or to continue to a doctoral program. Our students in the M.S. program have gone on to be very successful in industry at major companies such as Google and Microsoft as well as startups. The M.S. can also be an excellent stepping stone for a Ph.D. program. Many of our M.S. students go on to be admitted into Ph.D. programs either here at UCSD or at another top university. The M.S. program is very competitive. We receive well over 3,000 applications each year.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science

Concentration name: Artificial Intelligence, Bioinformatics, Computer Engineering (including VLSI, architecture, compilers, and parallel and distributed computing), Computer Graphics and Vision, Database Systems, Programming Languages, Compilers, and Software Engineering, Robotics, Security and Cryptography, Systems and Networking, Theoretical Computer Science
description: The CSE Ph.D. program is a research-based program with the goal to develop students for a career in research or academia. Students in the Ph.D. program will complete coursework, pass a qualifying exam, conduct research under the guidance of a faculty advisor, write and defend a thesis dissertation. The normal time to completion is five years.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science

description: The M.S. in Computer Science with a Specialization in Human-Centered Design (HCD) prepares students to be leaders in the research and design of next-generation human-computer interactions. The program is a collaboration between the Departments of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Cognitive Science (Cogs), and Communication (Comm). Students will take classes in all three departments, learning the theories, methods, and principles needed to design, implement, and evaluate technology from a human-centered perspective. The HCD specialization prepares students for careers as user experience (UX) researchers, interaction designers, usability engineers, and software developers at companies across the globe. Students are required to take five core classes, as well as a selection of electives, and can complete the degree by thesis or comprehensive exam.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science with a Specialization in Human-Centered Design

description: The CSE department offers a Ph.D. in Computer Science with a specialization in Human-Centered Design. Human-Centered Design is a creative, problem-solving process that seeks to create technology that is useful, usable, and desirable. The specialization includes courses and research opportunities with faculty in CSE and other departments. The program offers a unique opportunity to conduct research in Human-Centered Design in the context of a world-class engineering department and university.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science with a Specialization in Human-Centered Design

description: The department offers a master of science in computer science and a master of science in computer engineering. Both degrees can be earned with a specialization in an area of computer science and engineering. This specialization is in addition to the master’s degree. The MS program is intended to be a terminal professional degree. However, students who have successfully completed the MS degree at UC San Diego and who have been admitted to the PhD program in computer science and engineering at UC San Diego will be able to substitute some of the course work taken for the MS degree for PhD degree requirements. For further information, see PhD in Computer Science and Engineering. Students will select a group of courses in their intended area of specialization. See the department website for additional information.
Program name: Master of Science in Computer Science (Computer Engineering)

description: The Department of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) offers a PhD degree in Computer Science with a specialization in Computer Engineering. The specialization in Computer Engineering focuses on the study of the theoretical and practical aspects of computer architecture, computer-aided design, embedded systems, VLSI, and computer networks. Students who pursue the specialization in Computer Engineering will gain a deep understanding of the principles of computer design and implementation, as well as the ability to apply these principles to solve real-world problems. The program is designed for students with a strong background in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in research, academia, and industry. The PhD program is designed to produce experts who can advance the state of the art in computer science and engineering through research, teaching, and innovation. The program is flexible and can be tailored to the individual interests of the student.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science (Computer Engineering)

description: Students in the CSE Ph.D. program may choose to pursue a Ph.D. in computer science or computer engineering with a specialization in human-centered design. The specialization is intended for students who are interested in the design, implementation, and evaluation of computer systems that are meant to be used by people. The specialization is a collaboration between the Departments of Computer Science and Engineering, Cognitive Science, and Communication. The program involves coursework in all three departments and a dissertation that is supervised by faculty from at least two of the departments.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science (Computer Engineering) with a Specialization in Human-Centered Design

description: The Departments of Computer Science and Engineering and Cognitive Science offer an interdisciplinary program of study leading to a Ph.D. in Computer Science with a Specialization in Cognitive Science. The program is designed to train students in both computer science and cognitive science and to prepare them for research careers that span both fields. Students in the program must satisfy the requirements of both departments. The program is administered by a joint committee of faculty from both departments.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science and Cognitive Science

description: The Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering with a Specialization in Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary program between the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the Bioinformatics and Systems Biology Interdepartmental Program. The program is for students who wish to pursue a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering and are interested in research that bridges the fields of computer science and life sciences. All students in this program are required to complete a series of courses in computer science, bioinformatics and life sciences as well as conduct thesis research at the interface of these fields. This program is administered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering. Students wishing to apply to this program must submit an application for the Computer Science and Engineering Ph.D. program (Program Code CS76) and select the Bioinformatics Specialization on the application.
Program name: PhD in Computer Science with a Specialization in Bioinformatics

description: The Master of Advanced Study (MAS) in Data Science and Engineering is designed to meet the needs of working professionals who want to develop deep expertise in data science and engineering to advance their careers. The MAS in Data Science and Engineering provides a rigorous, hands-on curriculum that encompasses both the principles of data science and the engineering skills needed to build and deploy large-scale data systems. Students will learn the latest techniques in machine learning, statistics, and data mining, as well as the fundamentals of data systems, including databases, distributed computing, and data visualization. The program culminates in a capstone project in which students work in teams to solve a real-world data science problem. The MAS in Data Science and Engineering is a part-time, self-supporting program that can be completed in two years. Courses are offered in the evenings and on weekends to accommodate the schedules of working professionals. Students will have the opportunity to interact with leading researchers and practitioners in data science and engineering, and to network with other professionals in the field. The program is offered jointly by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the San Diego Supercomputer Center. Students will have access to the state-of-the-art computing resources of the San Diego Supercomputer Center, and will have the opportunity to work with real-world datasets from a variety of domains. The program prepares students for careers as data scientists, data engineers, and data analysts in a wide range of industries, including technology, finance, healthcare, and e-commerce. Graduates will be equipped with the skills and knowledge to design, build, and deploy data-driven solutions to the challenges of Big Data.
Program name: Master of Advanced Studies in Data Science and Engineering

description:
The Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (Advanced Manufacturing) program is a specialized professional master's degree program that prepares students for careers in this rapidly growing and dynamic field. Advanced manufacturing is an emerging field that requires significant interdisciplinary engineering training. The program is designed to attract and produce highly skilled engineers who are motivated to be the future leaders in the industry. It builds on the existing academic excellence of the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering, and its close ties with the local and global manufacturing industry, and is a unique addition to the portfolio of engineering disciplines at UC San Diego.

The goal of this innovative program is to produce forward-thinking engineers who will be able to design, build, and manage the advanced manufacturing systems of tomorrow. These systems will rely on sophisticated automation and integrated information technologies that blur the line between bits and atoms. Students in the program will study at the intersection of information technologies, intelligent systems, sensing and control, and manufacturing practices. The curriculum includes four core courses that cover all aspects of advanced manufacturing: design, processes, automation, and supply chains. In addition, students have several technical electives to choose from to build technical depth in their areas of interest, such as additive manufacturing, advanced materials, robotics and automation, and supply chain management. The M.S. program also includes an invaluable internship with a local or global manufacturing company that will give students real-world experience.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (Advanced Manufacturing)
Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Applied Electromagnetics)

description: The Ph.D. program is strongly research-oriented and is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research and/or university-level teaching. An M.S. degree is not a prerequisite for admission to the Ph.D. program. Holders of a B.S. degree in engineering, science, or mathematics are eligible to apply. The ECE department offers graduate programs leading to the Ph.D. degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering. The Ph.D. degree is a research degree, which requires the completion of an approved program of study and a dissertation. The dissertation must be a significant contribution of new knowledge based on the candidate's original research.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Applied Electromagnetics)

description: The ECE department at UCSD offers graduate education and research in a master's degree program in Electrical Engineering (Applied Ocean Sciences), MS. This program is in collaboration with the graduate programs at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO). The program is targeted at students interested in the observational and theoretical aspects of ocean science. This includes the study of ocean acoustics, optics, electromagnetics, geophysics, and oceanography. Applicants should select the department code ECE and the major code EE83 Electrical Engineering (Applied Ocean Sciences).
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Applied Ocean Sciences)

description: The Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering (Applied Ocean Sciences) is a unique, interdepartmental program offered in conjunction with the Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), which is a graduate division of UC San Diego. The program is devoted to the application of electrical engineering principles to oceanography. The program of study combines the core curriculum of the Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) Department with a wide choice of electives in applied ocean sciences. Applicants must have an undergraduate degree in engineering, physics or mathematics.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Applied Ocean Sciences)

description: The M.S. concentration in Applied Physics combines a core ECE graduate curriculum with a flexible set of electives offered by the ECE, Physics, and Nano/Mechanical Engineering Departments. The program is designed to provide students with a broad and inter-disciplinary background to pursue a career in industry or further their studies in a Ph.D. program. The curriculum focuses on the fundamentals of materials science, electromagnetism, and quantum mechanics, and their applications to modern electronic and photonic devices and nanotechnology. Students are expected to complete 49 units, including 13 units of core courses, 24 units of electives and a 12-unit research project. The project is supervised by a faculty member, and culminates in a final report and an oral presentation.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Applied Physics)

description: The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) offers graduate programs leading to the MS, and PhD degrees in Electrical Engineering. The department has 56 faculty and over 600 graduate students. ECE has a selective graduate admissions process which seeks to identify and admit students who have the interest, motivation, and academic preparation to succeed. The PhD program is a research-based program which requires a dissertation. The Applied Physics program is for students interested in the physical basis of modern and future electronic and photonic devices and systems. Specific topics include: magnetism and magnetic recording; novel electronic materials and devices; opto-electronic devices and displays; high-speed optical communications; and quantum electronics and computation.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Applied Physics)

description: The Communication Theory and Systems (CTS) major area of study is concerned with the theory and practice of communication systems. Examples include wireless systems (cellular, WiFi, satellite, ad-hoc networks, internet of things), data storage and magnetic recording systems, and communication over the optical fiber network which forms the backbone of the internet. The subject is based on a solid foundation of random process theory and digital signal processing, which are core areas of the program. The curriculum covers the transmission of information in both digital and analog format, and includes the study of coding for data compression and error correction, modulation and demodulation, wireless channel modeling, statistical signal processing, information theory, and network protocols and architecture.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Communication Theory and Systems)

description: The Communication Theory and Systems (CTS) major at UC San Diego's Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) Department is a premier graduate program renowned for its groundbreaking research and exceptional faculty. At CTS, we delve into the fundamental principles that underpin modern communication technologies, from wireless networks and data storage to optical communications and information theory. Our distinguished faculty members are leaders in their respective fields, actively pushing the boundaries of knowledge and mentoring the next generation of innovators. Students in the CTS program engage in cutting-edge research projects, collaborate with industry partners, and benefit from a vibrant academic community that fosters intellectual curiosity and professional growth. Whether you aspire to a career in academia, research, or industry, the CTS major provides the rigorous training and invaluable resources to help you achieve your goals and make a lasting impact on the world of communications.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Communication Theory and Systems)

description: The M.S. and Ph.D. programs are in Electrical and Computer Engineering. Within the ECE department there are 9 different specializations (depths), with the degree being awarded in Electrical Engineering. They are: Applied Ocean Science (no M.S. degree); Applied Physics-Electronic Devices and Materials; Communication Theory and Systems; Computer Engineering; Electronic Circuits and Systems; Intelligent Systems, Robotics and Control; Medical Devices and Systems; Nanoscale Devices and Systems; Photonics; Signal and Image Processing.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Computer Engineering)

description: The ECE department offers graduate programs leading to the Master of Science (MS) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Electrical and Computer Engineering. The department is part of the Jacobs School of Engineering. The PhD program is strongly research-oriented and is for students whose goal is to pursue a career in research and/or university-level teaching. An MS degree is not required to be admitted into the PhD program. We do not offer a separate Master's degree program to PhD students; a Master's degree may be awarded as a secondary degree.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Computer Engineering)

description: The Electronic Circuits and Systems (ECS) group is concerned with the analysis, and design of analog, mixed-signal (analog/digital), and radio-frequency (RF) integrated circuits and systems, as well as digital electronic circuits and systems. This includes the fields of analog and RF integrated circuits and systems, data converters (A/D and D/A), high-speed digital and mixed-signal integrated circuits, wireline and wireless communications transceivers, power management circuits, biosensors and bioelectronics, and VLSI. The curriculum of the ECS group is built around a core of courses on analog, digital, and RF integrated circuits and systems.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Circuits and Systems)

description: The ECE department at UC San Diego has a graduate research program that is among the most distinguished in the country. Our PhD students have unparalleled access to the resources of a major research university, including faculty who are leading experts in their fields, and state-of-the-art research facilities and laboratories. The ECE PhD program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills to become the next generation of innovators, researchers, and educators who will make a profound and lasting impact on society.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Circuits and Systems)

description: This area deals with the fundamentals of intelligent systems, including the theory and application of robotics, computer vision, control systems, and machine learning. Specific topics include: linear and nonlinear systems, optimal, adaptive, and robust control; estimation and identification; robotics; computer vision; pattern recognition; and machine learning. Applications include: autonomous vehicles (including ground, marine, and air), manufacturing, and biomedical devices.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Intelligent Systems, Robotics, and Control)

description: The ECE PhD program is designed to provide students with the advanced skills and knowledge needed to be a leader in their chosen area of research, whether that be in academia or industry. The PhD degree is a research degree and is granted upon the successful completion of a program of study that includes a dissertation based on original research in a specialty of Electrical and Computer Engineering. The Intelligent Systems, Robotics, and Control area deals with the theory and application of optimization, autonomous systems, and machine learning. Topics include: control of complex dynamical systems, reinforcement learning, convex and non-convex optimization, robotic motion planning and control, machine learning, computer vision, pattern recognition, and image and video processing. Applications include: robotics, autonomous vehicles, cyber-physical systems, data science, wireless communication networks, power grids, and biomedical systems.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Intelligent Systems, Robotics, and Control)

description: The Electrical and Computer Engineering department at UC San Diego is a large and multi-faceted department and we are lucky to have many faculty that are conducting research in the general area of Machine Learning and Data Science. The Machine Learning and Data Science M.S. program is inter-disciplinary in nature and we encourage students to explore a broad range of topics including computer vision, robotics, statistical and cognitive modeling, natural language processing, speech and text processing, computational biology, etc. Our students have the freedom to develop their own individualized M.S. curriculum with the help of a faculty adviser. The program culminates in a final capstone project, the successful completion of which will demonstrate that the student has acquired the tools and techniques of the field.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Machine Learning and Data Science)

description: Machine learning and data science has emerged as a central discipline in engineering that is revolutionizing a wide-range of industries including health, transportation, and e-commerce. It uses ideas from statistics, optimization, and algorithms to enable computers to learn from data in order to make predictions and decisions. The ECE department has an outstanding group of faculty with research that spans the full range of activities in ML and its applications, including active learning, classification, clustering, computational photography, computer vision, deep learning, dimensionality reduction, reinforcement learning, graphical models, robotics, statistical learning, and video processing.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Machine Learning and Data Science)

description: The ECE department offers a Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering. Within the M.S. degree program, the department offers a specialization in Medical Devices and Systems. This M.S. specialization is intended for students who are interested in applying electrical and computer engineering to healthcare and medicine. The specialization covers a broad range of topics in medical technology, including medical device design, medical imaging, and healthcare data analytics. The specialization is well-suited for students who plan to pursue an industrial career in the medical technology field, as well as those who wish to pursue a doctoral degree in a related area.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Medical Devices and Systems)

description: This research area focuses on the design, development, and application of new devices and methods for the diagnosis and treatment of human diseases, and for the study of fundamental biological processes. The research is highly interdisciplinary, and involves faculty from ECE, Bioengineering, Medicine, and Radiology. The research interests of the faculty can be divided into four main areas: Biomedical imaging (e.g., MRI, ultrasound, optical imaging, X-ray computed tomography); Cardiovascular engineering (e.g., sensors and systems for monitoring and treating cardiovascular diseases); Neuro-engineering (e.g., neural interfaces, neural recording and stimulation, neural signal processing); and Wireless and mobile health (e.g., body-area networks, wearable sensors, wireless powering and data telemetry). Research in this area involves the design of sensors and instrumentation, the development of algorithms for signal/image processing and machine learning, and pre-clinical and/or clinical evaluation. ECE students working in this area interact closely with students and faculty from the Bioengineering Department, School of Medicine, and the Health Sciences.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Medical Devices and Systems)

description: The Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Medical Imaging) is a joint interdepartmental program offered by the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering and the Department of Bioengineering at the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering, and the Department of Radiology at the UC San Diego School of Medicine. The program is designed to train leaders in the development and application of medical imaging technologies. It addresses the needs of three groups of students: (1) students who seek a terminal master’s degree to work in industry or as specialized technicians in academic or medical research laboratories; (2) students with a bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline who wish to obtain a master’s degree in engineering before entering medical school; and (3) students who wish to obtain an MS degree before pursuing a PhD.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Medical Imaging)

description: A special multidisciplinary program in medical imaging is offered, leading to a PhD in electrical and computer engineering (medical imaging). This PhD program is intended for students with an undergraduate degree in an engineering discipline or in the physical/biological sciences. The program is administered by the ECE department, and the degree is in electrical and computer engineering (medical imaging).
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Medical Imaging)

description: The NDS depth area is for students interested in the materials, device physics, design, and fabrication of electronic, optoelectronic, and MEMS devices and systems. The coursework and research of the faculty in this group encompasses a wide range of topics that are critical to future technologies. The group has strong programs in traditional areas of silicon devices and materials but is best known for its innovative research in new areas such as nanotechnology, advanced displays, organic electronics, and novel MEMS devices. There is a strong emphasis on the design, fabrication, and characterization of these novel devices and materials using the state-of-the-art facilities of the Nano3 Cleanroom.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Nanoscale Devices and Systems)

description: The Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) department offers a doctor of philosophy (PhD) degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering. The PhD degree is a research degree requiring a dissertation. The requirements for the PhD degree consist of completing a research project that is substantial enough to be published in a peer-reviewed academic conference or journal, writing a dissertation describing the research, and a public oral defense of the dissertation. In addition, students in the PhD program are required to complete a course requirement and a series of three examinations.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Nanoscale Devices and Systems)

description: The M.S. specialization in Photonics provides interdisciplinary training in photonics systems and technology, with applications including, but not limited to, communications, sensing, and imaging. The curriculum integrates topics of optical physics, devices, and systems. The program provides the theoretical and hands-on-training needed for a professional career. All students are required to take ECE 221 and ECE 223. Students are encouraged to take a laboratory course ECE 225A, B, C, or D. It is also recommended that each student should plan to take at least one course in each of the three sub-disciplines: Optical Physics, Devices, and Systems. The courses that fall within these sub-disciplines are listed below.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Photonics)

description: The Electrical and Computer Engineering Department offers graduate programs leading to the MS and PhD degrees in Electrical and Computer Engineering. The department has five main research groups, organized by research area and curriculum. Photonics is one of the five areas. Photonics includes the science and technology of generating and harnessing light and other forms of radiant energy whose quantum unit is the photon. The Photonics research group focuses on nanophotonics and biophotonics, displays, memories, energy and green-photonics, optical interconnects, silicon photonics, high power lasers, optical metrology, imaging, nonlinear optics, quantum optics and quantum computing, novel optical materials, etc. PhD students are assigned a faculty research adviser in their first quarter of study, and students pursue a program of study under the direction of their faculty adviser. The program of study is tailored to the individual student's needs and interests. The goal is to provide students with the background and skills needed to become successful, independent researchers.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Photonics)

description: The Signal and Image Processing (SIP) program offers a rich multi-disciplinary learning and research environment. The world-renowned faculty, state-of-the-art research laboratories, and strong ties to the local high-tech industry offer a vibrant academic environment for graduate students. The SIP Program focuses on the theory, design and application of digital signal processing, including digital image and video processing, digital communications, computer vision, and pattern recognition. Students learn the fundamentals of signal processing and specialize in one or more of these advanced areas. Beyond the fundamentals, graduate students are exposed to and can participate in cutting-edge research in a large variety of topics, including: digital image and video processing and coding; computer vision; pattern recognition and machine learning; multi-media systems; audio and music signal processing; communication systems and networks; information theory; and VLSI and architectures for signal processing. Our graduates not only have a solid foundation in the fundamental principles of signal and image processing, but also possess the research and problem solving skills that are necessary to tackle complex engineering problems, as well as the ability to work in teams.
Program name: Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (Signal and Image Processing)

description: The Signal and Image Processing (SIP) group at UC San Diego is a part of the Electrical and Computer Engineering department, and is affiliated with the Center for Wireless Communications, the Center for Magnetic Recording Research, the California Institute of Telecommunications and Information Technology, the San Diego Supercomputer Center, and the Swartz Center for Computational Neuroscience. The group conducts research in many areas, including audio and speech processing, image and video processing and compression, biomedical signal processing, information theory, statistical signal processing, and machine learning. Students working in this area can get a specialization in Signal and Image Processing.
Program name: PhD in Electrical Engineering (Signal and Image Processing)

Concentration name: communications and information engineering, computational science and engineering, computer engineering, electromagnetics, electronic materials and devices, intelligent systems and controls, optics and photonics, and signal and image processing
description: The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UC San Diego and the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at San Diego State University jointly offer a program of study leading to the Doctor of Philosophy degree in Engineering Sciences (Electrical and Computer Engineering). This program is administered by the Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) Executive Committee and provides students with access to the combined faculty, facilities, and curricula of both institutions. The program is best suited for students who are interested in pursuing interdisciplinary research that is supported by faculty at both institutions. Research specializations include communications and information engineering, computational science and engineering, computer engineering, electromagnetics, electronic materials and devices, intelligent systems and controls, optics and photonics, and signal and image processing. The program aims to train a new generation of engineers who can seamlessly work in, and bridge the gap between, academia and industry.
Program name: PhD in Engineering Sciences (Electrical and Computer Engineering) (Joint with San Diego State University)

description: The Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) program in Wireless Embedded Systems is geared towards meeting the needs of working professionals in the embedded systems industry. The program provides an interdisciplinary curriculum spanning the fields of communication theory, computer science, and electrical engineering. The curriculum provides a broad educational experience, covering the fundamentals of real-time embedded systems, as well as state-of-the-art specialization tracks in a variety of application areas. The curriculum for the M.A.S. program is designed to be completed in two years of part-time study. Students must complete 36 units of coursework, which includes a team-based capstone project. Students must maintain a 3.0 grade-point average to graduate.
Program name: Master of Advanced Studies in Wireless Embedded Systems

description: The Master of Arts in Economics is a full-time terminal master’s program with an emphasis on applied microeconomics, big data, and quantitative methods. A key objective of our program is to equip students with practical skills and state-of-the-art knowledge, with which to be successful as an economist or data analyst in the private or public sector. To this end, our program focuses on topics such as econometrics, applied microeconomics, and computation for economics and big data. Students will develop skills in data analysis and econometric modeling as well as learning to use state-of-the-art statistical software, such as Matlab, Stata, and R.
