We are a designated STEM program (CIP Code 45.0603: Econometrics and Quantitative Economics). Students with F-1 visas are eligible to apply for a 24-month STEM optional practical training (OPT) extension.
Program name: Master of Arts in Economics

description: The Ph.D. program in Economics at UC San Diego is a 5-year program designed to train students to be professional economists. The department looks to admit 25-30 students per year. Our graduates have been very successful in securing excellent jobs. You can see a list of our initial placements for the last few years. The first year of the program is devoted to core classes in Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, and Econometrics. These classes provide the basic tools for all economists. At the end of the first year, students take qualifying exams in each of these three areas. In the second and third years, students take field courses to gain expertise in a smaller number of areas. A list of our fields can be found here. Starting in the summer after the first year, students will start working on their own research. The second year paper is due at the start of the third year. This is typically a student's first research paper and is a major requirement for the program. The third year paper is due at the start of the fourth year. This paper is also a major requirement for the program. The fourth and fifth years of the program are devoted to research for the dissertation. The final job market paper is presented at the beginning of the fall quarter of the student's fifth year.
Program name: PhD in Economics

Concentration name: Single Subject: Science (Biology, Chemistry, Earth Science, or Physics)
description: The M.Ed./Credential Program at UC San Diego is a full-time, two-year course of study that results in a Master of Education degree and a California Preliminary Multiple Subject or Single Subject Teaching Credential. We prepare future teachers to be educational leaders who are committed to equity and social justice. We admit a diverse group of students into a small cohort who work closely with faculty in a supportive and collaborative environment throughout their two years in the program. Students develop a strong foundation in educational theory and practice through a combination of coursework and fieldwork placements in local K-12 schools. Our unique program design allows students to apply what they learn in their university courses in their fieldwork classrooms right away. Upon completion of the program, graduates are prepared to be thoughtful and reflective practitioners who can meet the needs of a wide range of students in diverse educational settings.
Accreditation status: The teacher credentialing programs at UC San Diego are accredited by the California Commission on Teacher Credentialing (CTC).
Program name: Master of Education (M.Ed.)

Concentration name: Transforming Learning, Schooling, and Human Development, Transforming Educational Policy and Social Inquiry, Transforming Mathematics and Science Education
description: The Ph.D. in Education: Transforming Education in a Diverse Society is offered as a department-based Ph.D. in Education Studies at UC San Diego. Students in this program are committed to understanding and addressing the educational challenges that face a diverse society. The program of study is interdisciplinary. It draws upon the social sciences, including anthropology, economics, history, political science, psychology and sociology. It is also informed by work in cognitive science, critical theory, cultural studies, discourse analysis, ethnic studies, language and linguistics, and sociolinguistics. The Ph.D. in Education prepares students to conduct research on the pressing educational issues of our time, and to bridge research and practice. In our program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary for a career in academia, in educational research, or in other leadership positions. All Ph.D. students specialize in one of three areas. They also must develop an interdisciplinary cognate by taking a series of courses outside of EDS.
Program name: PhD in Education

description: The MFA in Acting is a three-year program designed for the student-actor who has a desire to become a skilled professional actor on stage or screen. Students are trained by faculty artists and scholars with a wealth of experience in the professional world and in academia. The program offers a demanding and intensive journey of artistic exploration and development for a select group of students, with emphasis on individual growth and the creation of a strong ensemble. It culminates with a professional residency in the final quarter of the program, at La Jolla Playhouse. The training nurtures a well-rounded artist who will be prepared for a career in the professional theatre world, in a variety of performance mediums. UC San Diego is a NAST accredited program.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Acting)

description: The MFA in Dance is a three-year program that offers graduate students the opportunity to concentrate on choreography and/or performance of contemporary dance. The curriculum supports the development of a strong personal artistic voice and an understanding of the artist's role in society. Courses in choreography, dance technique, performance, teaching, and dance studies are required. Students are provided with regular opportunities to create and show their work, and perform in faculty and student choreographed concerts. The program concludes with a final creative project, which can be a thesis performance of original choreography and/or a performance of a major role. Graduate students have the opportunity to serve as a Teaching Assistant, teaching classes in dance technique, dance studies and/or introductory courses for non-majors. This experience provides essential training for a career in academia.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Dance Theatre)

description:
The MFA Design Program at UC San Diego is a three-year program for students who intend to pursue a career as a professional designer in theatre, dance, or other live performance genres. The design program provides an environment where design faculty and students form a community of artists who work together and share a passion for the creation of new works. The program's proximity to a major theatre city allows for regular interaction with professional artists and theatres, which helps to foster an understanding of the current demands of the profession.

The curriculum is flexible and individually tailored, combining rigorous training with an emphasis on new work and new technology. Practical production work is an integral part of the graduate design training program, with each student designing in all four areas (costume, lighting, scenic, sound) for fully-mounted productions in the department's season. In addition, students will have the opportunity to serve as an assistant to a faculty or guest designer.

All graduate students have opportunities to collaborate on projects with MFA directors and playwrights, as well as with students from the PhD program in Theatre and Drama, a joint program with UC Irvine. Design students also collaborate with choreographers in the dance program.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Design)

description:
The three-year Directing program at UC San Diego is a selective and rigorous program dedicated to the artistic, intellectual and professional development of the emerging stage director.

Through a combination of seminars, studio classes, and a robust production season, directors will develop their individual voice and aesthetic while acquiring the necessary skills to lead a creative team through the process of making theatre.

Directors are guaranteed a production slot in the season in each of their three years. These projects are cast from the MFA acting cohort and are fully supported by the department's team of professional designers, stage managers and technicians.

In addition to the practical experience of directing in the season, students will assist faculty and guest directors on department productions, work as a teaching assistant for undergraduate courses, and may pursue independent study projects and internships with our professional theatre partners.

Directors will also have the opportunity to serve as producers of the annual Wagner New Play Festival, a department-wide celebration of new work by our graduate playwrights. In the Festival, each director will be paired with a playwright and will direct a workshop production of a new play.

At the conclusion of their third year, students will present their work in a showcase for industry professionals in Los Angeles and New York.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Directing)

description:
The MFA playwriting program at UC San Diego is a three-year, intensive writing program. We only admit one or two writers a year. The small class size allows us to provide each writer with the individual attention his/her/their work requires. The program is committed to the idea that the theatre is a writer's medium and that the most exciting and vital theatre is created by artists who are passionate, disciplined and engaged in the world-at-large. Students write a full-length play each quarter. Each of these plays has at least a staged reading and some are given a workshop production. Every student will receive at least one production in the Wagner New Play Festival in the third year. All students are eligible to be chosen to receive a mainstage production in the department's subscription season.

The first year focuses on the fundamentals of dramatic writing through weekly writing assignments and the reading of a wide range of plays from the Greeks to the present day. The second year focuses on developing and deepening the writer’s voice and vision. In addition to playwriting workshops, seminars are offered in such subjects as theory and criticism, classical and contemporary drama, screenwriting and television writing, and teaching playwriting. Second- and third-year writers mentor undergraduate playwriting students. All playwriting students meet as a group once a week with the head of playwriting to discuss their work and other subjects of interest.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Playwriting)

description:
The UC San Diego Stage Management program is a three year, residency-based program designed to provide a select group of students with the opportunity to acquire the skills and training needed to become a leader in the theatre. It is a rigorous and comprehensive curriculum that combines classroom instruction with a strong emphasis on production work.

In the first year of training, students learn the fundamentals of stage management and serve as an assistant stage manager on at least two productions.

The second year focuses on honing the stage management skills of calling a show, managing a rehearsal room and functioning as the hub of communication. The second-year student will stage manage at least two productions.

Third year students stage manage one production and work on a professional residency at a theatre of their choice, such as La Jolla Playhouse or a regional theatre.
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Stage Management)

description: The joint Ph.D. program in drama and theatre between UC Irvine and UC San Diego offers students a unique course of study that combines the scholarly and research resources of two internationally ranked doctoral programs. Students in the joint program pursue a curriculum that is designed to provide a strong theoretical, historical and global foundation for their individual research. In addition to regular coursework on both campuses, students have the opportunity to participate in department productions, UC-wide conferences, faculty-led research projects, and the publication of TheatreForum, an international journal of theatre and performance.
Program name: PhD in Drama and Theatre (Joint Program with UC Irvine)

description: The joint PhD program in Drama and Theatre between UC San Diego and UC Irvine offers students a unique course of study that combines the scholarly and pedagogical resources of two internationally-recognized departments and faculties. The program admits a small number of students each year for a curriculum that is designed to be completed in five years of residency. Students are typically admitted to and affiliated with a home campus, either UC San Diego or UC Irvine, and during their coursework they are in residence for one year at the other UC campus. During this year of residency, they take seminars, work with faculty and are fully integrated into the life of the other department. Courses on both campuses are available to all students in the program throughout their residency. The program is interdisciplinary in its orientation and it encourages students to develop a course of study that integrates the critical, historical, and theoretical dimensions of theatre and performance studies. The Department of Theatre and Dance is a participating department in the graduate specialization in Critical Gender Studies. The specialization provides specialized training in gender, sexuality, and queer studies for students currently enrolled in a UC San Diego doctoral program. The specialization is designed to complement students’ disciplinary training, introduce them to the central questions and methodologies of CGS as an interdisciplinary field, and provide a credential that will be legible to future employers. Admitted students are required to complete five courses (two core courses and three electives) and to include a chapter on a CGS-related topic in their doctoral dissertation. Upon successful completion of all requirements, students will receive a certificate of completion and the following notation on their transcript: 'Specialization in Critical Gender Studies.'
Program name: PhD in Drama and Theatre with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies (Joint with UC Irvine)

description: The graduate program in History at UC San Diego is a vibrant intellectual community of faculty and students who share a commitment to historical research and analysis. Our distinguished faculty train graduate students to become scholars and teachers of the highest caliber. We offer programs of study leading to the Master of Arts (MA) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Our areas of expertise include the history of the United States, Europe, Latin America, East Asia, the ancient Near East, the Middle East, and Science, Technology, and Medicine. The Department of History does not have a terminal M.A. program. The Master of Arts degree is awarded under one of three circumstances: 1. It is a prerequisite for doctoral candidates, and is based on a research paper (equivalent to a Master's Thesis) and a comprehensive written examination on a major and a minor field. 2. A student may be awarded a terminal master's degree in lieu of the PhD after successful completion of all requirements for the PhD except for the dissertation. 3. A terminal MA may be granted to students in the PhD program who for various reasons are not able to complete the doctoral degree.
Program name: Master of Arts in History

description: The graduate program in History at the University of California, San Diego, offers a Ph.D. in a wide variety of fields. The department is committed to training graduate students for careers in research and teaching. All students admitted to the doctoral program are guaranteed five years of funding, including tuition, fees, and a stipend. We have a strong record of placing our students in tenure-track academic positions, postdoctoral fellowships, and a wide range of other professions. We encourage you to look through our website, especially the information about our faculty and graduate students, to get a better sense of who we are and what we do.
Program name: PhD in History

description: The two-year, full-time Master of International Affairs (MIA) degree program at UC San Diego’s School of Global Policy and Strategy (GPS) is for those who seek a professional career in international affairs. Students develop invaluable analytical skills to examine a wide range of global issues and are prepared for a variety of careers in the international arena in the public, private and nonprofit sectors. The MIA program’s curriculum blends international relations, international political economy, public policy and management. All students are required to choose both a regional and career track specialization.
Program name: Master of International Affairs

description: The Master of Public Policy (MPP) is a two-year, full-time professional degree program that is a member of the Association of Professional Schools of International Affairs (APSIA). The curriculum is built upon a set of core courses that give students a solid foundation in public policy analysis. Our students learn to take on a broad range of policy challenges in the U.S. and around the globe. The School of Global Policy and Strategy’s (GPS) MPP program is a STEM-designated degree program in Econometrics and Quantitative Economics (CIP Code 45.0603). Students with F-1 visas will be eligible to apply for a 24-month optional practical training (OPT) extension.
Program name: Master of Public Policy

description: The Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Educational Leadership at the University of California San Diego (UC San Diego) and California State University San Marcos (CSUSM) is a unique program that brings together the resources of two outstanding universities to offer a terminal degree in educational leadership. The program is designed to prepare a new generation of P-12 and postsecondary educational leaders who will be able to respond to the challenges of a pluralistic and globally-interconnected society. The Ed.D. in Transformational Leadership program offers students a timely, relevant and personalized experience. The program is designed for working professionals with a minimum of 5 years of leadership experience and uses a cohort model. Students begin the program each year in the summer and take classes for 3 consecutive years including summers.
Program name: Doctor of Education in Transformational Leadership (Ed.D.)

Concentration name: Disciplinary concentration (Anthropology, Communication, History, Literature, Political Science, Sociology) and a thematic focus (Cultural Studies, Gender Studies, International Migration, Public Health, or U.S.-Mexico Relations)
description: The Master of Arts in Latin American Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide a broad-based, integrated understanding of contemporary Latin America. The program offers both a terminal M.A. degree for students who wish to pursue careers in the private or public sector, and a comprehensive M.A. for those who wish to continue their studies at the doctoral level. The program provides students with the intellectual tools for understanding the region, its people, and its cultures, as well as the challenges facing its societies. In the core curriculum, students study historical and contemporary issues facing Latin America from the perspectives of several different disciplines. They then select a disciplinary concentration (Anthropology, Communication, History, Literature, Political Science, Sociology) and a thematic focus (Cultural Studies, Gender Studies, International Migration, Public Health, or U.S.-Mexico Relations). Students may elect to pursue either Plan I (Thesis) or Plan II (Comprehensive Examination). Both are two-year programs. To earn the M.A. degree, students must demonstrate proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese, and complete a minimum of twelve courses (48 units). Students must receive a grade of B or better in all coursework to receive credit.
Program name: Master of Arts in Latin American Studies

description: The M.A. program is a two-year program intended to provide students with a solid foundation in the main areas of linguistics (phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics), training in research methods and opportunities for independent research. The program is designed to be a stepping stone to a PhD program in linguistics or a related field. It does not provide training for careers in translation, interpretation, or language teaching. The department does not offer a terminal M.A.
Program name: Master of Arts in Linguistics

description: The graduate program in linguistics at UC San Diego is a research-oriented program leading to the PhD degree. The department has a strong focus on theoretical linguistics, in the domains of syntax, semantics, phonology, and phonetics. The approach to linguistics is interdisciplinary, with an emphasis on the empirical foundations of linguistic theory. The department has a long-standing tradition of research in a wide variety of languages. Laboratory research is a key component of the doctoral program, with experimental work in phonetics, phonology, syntax, semantics, and language acquisition conducted in the department’s various labs. Students also have the option to pursue research on the linguistic structure of signed languages and on the neural bases of language. Close instructional and research connections exist with the Department of Cognitive Science, the Department of Communication, the Center for Research in Language, the Institute for Neural Computation, and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies. The interdisciplinary nature of research in linguistics is also supported by joint appointments of some Linguistics faculty in other departments, as well as through coursework and research opportunities in allied disciplines.
Program name: PhD in Linguistics

description: The M.A. in Literature is a one-year degree that provides students an opportunity for concentrated study in a particular area of literature. The M.A. has three central components: a focused program of coursework, training in pedagogy, and a final portfolio project. Students may use the M.A. to prepare for a variety of professions, from teaching to publishing, or to prepare for applying to Ph.D. programs in literature and related fields. UCSD undergraduates may apply to our B.A./M.A. program.
Program name: Master of Arts in Literature

description: The Literature Department at UC San Diego has from its beginning been committed to the study of literature and culture in a broad comparative and theoretical frame. Our graduate program is unique in its emphasis on historical and critical thinking and its attention to a wide range of languages and literatures. We do not have separate departments of English, Spanish, French, etc. Instead, our faculty is organized into language sections that include Chinese, English, French, German, Greek, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Russian, and Spanish. Our graduate students are also admitted into a language section where they are expected to do a substantial portion of their work. At the same time, we have a common curriculum for all students and faculty that is designed to train them as comparatists with a strong theoretical and historical grounding. Our focus on literary study is complemented by a rich and varied engagement with philosophy, history, and social and political thought, as well as with film and media studies, gender studies, and ethnic studies. This combination of linguistic rigor, comparative breadth, and theoretical sophistication has given our program a distinctive cast and a leading place in the country.
Program name: PhD in Literature

description: The Materials Science and Engineering Program (MATS) at UC San Diego is an interdisciplinary program that offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Materials Science and Engineering. The program brings together faculty from across the university, including the Departments of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Structural Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, NanoEngineering, Chemistry and Biochemistry, and Physics. Research in MATS focuses on the discovery of novel materials, and the understanding of the interrelationship between the selection, processing, structure, properties, and performance of materials, for the purpose of advancing engineering and scientific applications. MATS has strong interdisciplinary research collaborations, and has particular strengths in the following research thrusts: Advanced Structural Materials; Electronic and Photonic Materials; Energy Materials; Biomaterials and Soft Materials; and Computational Materials Science.
Program name: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The doctoral program in Materials Science and Engineering (PhD) is a research-oriented doctoral degree program. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the basic science of materials with opportunities to specialize in a particular area of materials science and engineering. Graduate students are trained for careers in academia, industry and national labs.
Program name: PhD in Materials Science and Engineering

description: The graduate program in mathematics at UC San Diego has, in its fifty year history, become a large and highly respected department. This is due to the high quality of the faculty and the students. The department has an international reputation for its work in a number of areas of both pure and applied mathematics. The department's graduate students are an important factor in its research life. Students are encouraged to become involved in research at an early stage. There are approximately one hundred fifty graduate students, and the small size of the advanced classes allows for a great deal of interaction between students and faculty. Students who perform well may be offered a teaching assistantship that provides a stipend and pays tuition and fees. Students from underrepresented groups who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents may be eligible for a San Diego fellowship. The department offers a terminal M.A. program with a specialization in statistics. Students in the M.A. program complete a set of qualifying exams for the Ph.D. program and then follow a course of study which enables them to write a thesis (Plan I) or take a comprehensive examination (Plan II). The M.A. programs prepare students for careers in government and industry, for teaching at the community college level, and for further study at the doctoral level in pure or applied mathematics.
Program name: Master of Arts in Mathematics

description: The M.S. in Mathematics is designed to be completed in one year, though students may take up to two years to complete their degree. The M.S. degree is offered in three specializations: Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, and Statistics. We offer two plans for the M.S. degree: Plan I (Thesis) and Plan II (Comprehensive Exam). All students are admitted into Plan II. Students who wish to switch to Plan I must find a thesis advisor and submit a Plan I request form by the end of their first quarter. Plan I is only recommended for students who plan to continue with a Ph.D. degree.
Program name: Master of Science in Mathematics

description: The graduate program in mathematics at UC San Diego has been ranked 19th among public universities and 34th overall among U.S. universities by U.S. News & World Report. The department faculty includes many pre-eminent mathematicians who have been recognized for their research by professional societies, prestigious fellowships, and other honors. The graduate program provides a rich and rewarding experience in a beautiful Southern California setting. With five required first-year courses in algebra, analysis, and topology, the program ensures students have a strong, broad foundation in mathematics. The remaining curriculum is flexible and can be tailored for each student's interests and goals. Students are encouraged to attend a variety of research seminars, starting in their first year. After passing the qualifying exams (typically in the second year), students begin to work closely with a faculty advisor. The department has active research groups in most areas of mathematics, including algebra, analysis, combinatorics, geometry, logic, number theory, numerical analysis, probability, and statistics.
Program name: PhD in Mathematics

description: The M.S. degree program is intended to provide students with an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge and competence in a particular area of mechanical and aerospace engineering and to develop experience in performing engineering research. The program is for qualified students who have a bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or a related field. There are two plans of study available, one with a thesis and one without. The M.S. program should be considered a preparatory step for students who wish to pursue a Ph.D. degree at UC San Diego, as the Ph.D. program requires a master’s degree for admission. Full time M.S. students are expected to complete their degree requirements by the end of their second year.
Program name: Master of Science in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

description: The MAE Ph.D. program is intended to prepare students for a career in research and/or academia. A key element of the Ph.D. program is the conduct of independent research under the supervision of a faculty advisor, culminating in the preparation and defense of a doctoral dissertation. We offer a wide range of cutting-edge research opportunities that span the breadth of modern mechanical and aerospace engineering. Our graduate students come from the best universities in the U.S. and around the world, and go on to become leaders in academia, industry and government.
Program name: PhD in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

description: The UC San Diego School of Medicine MD degree program is a four-year program that provides comprehensive education in the art and science of medicine. Our curriculum is designed to prepare students for a career in any field of medicine, with a strong emphasis on primary care and the needs of underserved communities. The program is divided into two phases: the pre-clerkship phase and the clerkship phase. In the pre-clerkship phase, students learn the foundational sciences of medicine, including anatomy, biochemistry, and physiology. In the clerkship phase, students rotate through various clinical specialties, such as internal medicine, pediatrics, and surgery.
Accreditation status: The University of California, San Diego School of Medicine is a fully accredited medical school. Our last accreditation site visit was in March 2022. We were granted continued full accreditation for an eight-year term by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME).
Program name: Doctor of Medicine (MD)

description: The graduate program in music at UC San Diego offers the degrees of Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) and Master of Arts (M.A.). The program is highly selective. It is not our goal to produce a large number of graduates but to provide an environment in which a few gifted individuals can pursue their musical interests and develop their skills to the fullest. We are interested in students who have already demonstrated significant achievement and who are dedicated to a life of continuing artistic and intellectual growth. The M.A. is a two-year degree with concentrations in Composition, Computer Music, or Integrative Studies. The M.A. program is designed for students who have not yet had sufficient background and training to be admitted to the Ph.D. program. The M.A. is also appropriate for those who wish to pursue a more limited course of study beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students are admitted to one of the three areas of concentration listed above.
Program name: Master of Arts in Music

description: The Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Contemporary Music Performance is offered by the Department of Music at UC San Diego. The program is unique in that it is a research-oriented doctoral program in performance, designed to be on a par with the Ph.D. The program aims to produce performers who are also scholars and scholar-performers who are also outstanding musicians. The program is intentionally small to allow for intensive contact between students and faculty. The department has a large and varied faculty in performance who work in a variety of musical styles with emphasis in contemporary music. Most performance faculty perform in the top professional new music ensembles in the San Diego area, including the San Diego Symphony, or are active as soloists and chamber musicians nationally and internationally. The program gives students a strong technical foundation on their instrument, experience in a wide range of repertoire, and the development of a personal artistic vision through in-depth study of music of the 20th and 21st centuries. Students will gain experience in a variety of performance situations, from solo and chamber music to large ensemble, and will be given opportunities to work with composers and to participate in the creation of new works. Students will have access to a wide variety of courses in the Department of Music, including courses in composition, computer music, and integrative studies.
Program name: Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA)

Concentration name: Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, Performance
description: The Ph.D. program in Music is an integrated degree with five specialized areas of study, referred to as 'research areas': Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, and Performance. It is a fundamental feature of the Department that these research areas are not separate departments, but interact on a daily basis. The focus of the program is on the creation of new music and the development of new ideas about music. Music at UCSD is understood to be an art of sound, and all sound is considered potential material for musical creation and inquiry. We do not privilege any one style or tradition of music making or study, and we encourage our graduate students to explore the rich variety of musics available to them. To this end we offer a strong faculty representing a wide array of musical interests. Our goal is to prepare graduate students to be the next generation of composers, performers, and scholars who will lead the field in the twenty-first century.
Program name: PhD in Music

description: The Neurosciences Graduate Program at UC San Diego is an inter-institutional program dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in neuroscience research, education, and outreach. The program spans more than 30 departments and sections across UC San Diego and three affiliated research institutes: the Salk Institute for Biological Studies, the Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute, and The Scripps Research Institute. Established in 1968, the program is the oldest and one of the largest neuroscience graduate programs in the country. Our more than 160 faculty provide an extraordinary breadth of research and training opportunities, in a collaborative and collegial atmosphere. Students receive five years of guaranteed financial support and typically complete their PhDs in an average of 5.5 years. The program is committed to a holistic admissions process, recognizing that a diverse and inclusive student body is a cornerstone of a preeminent graduate program.
Program name: PhD in Neurosciences

description: The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences at UC San Diego offers a four-year Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) degree program that is committed to providing an innovative and flexible curriculum in a highly inter-disciplinary environment. The curriculum is taught by a unique blend of faculty from the School of Pharmacy, the UC San Diego School of Medicine and other campus departments. The program focuses on the students' development as future leaders in pharmacy by providing opportunities for inter-professional collaborations in patient care, leadership roles in professional organizations, and specialized elective streams that are tailored to the students' career goals. The small class size, paired with San Diego's collaborative biotech and medical environment, allows for a personalized and team-oriented experience which prepares students to be successful leaders in patient care, research, and industry.
Accreditation status: The University of California San Diego Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences’ Doctor of Pharmacy program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education, 190 South LaSalle Street, Suite 3000, Chicago, IL 60603, 312/664-3575; FAX 866/228-2631, web site www.acpe-accredit.org.
Program name: Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.)

description: The Master of Science in Drug Development and Product Management is a one-year, in-person master’s degree program that provides students with a multidisciplinary education to meet the needs of the pharmaceutical industry. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the key knowledge and skills that are essential to transition to a career in drug development and product management. Students will learn the process of how a drug or a product moves from the laboratory to the marketplace from world-renowned faculty at the University of California San Diego. Students will also experience hands-on training via the capstone course where they will learn from and interact with industry leaders in drug development, clinical trials, business development and project management. The curriculum also provides students with the training in professional development to support successful career placement following graduation.
Program name: Master of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences

description: The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences offers a PhD degree program in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences. The doctoral degree program provides a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of drug discovery, drug delivery and drug action, and prepares students for a variety of careers in academia, the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, as well as government. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, offers training in diverse areas of pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences, and fosters collaborations between students and faculty in different specializations. The Skaggs School of Pharmacy is part of UC San Diego Health Sciences, which also includes the School of Medicine, the Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science, and UC San Diego Health. UC San Diego Health Sciences is an innovative, collaborative, and highly translational environment for biomedical research.
Program name: PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences

description: The department offers a terminal M.A. program in philosophy. The M.A. is designed to be completed in one year (three quarters) of full-time study. The program is designed for students who can benefit from a year of graduate-level work in philosophy. Some students enter the program to deepen their knowledge of philosophy before applying to Ph.D. programs, while others are interested in the connections between philosophy and their undergraduate major or profession. Still others are drawn to the program out of an interest in philosophy and a desire to pursue it at a more advanced level. The M.A. program has been very successful at preparing students for admission to Ph.D. programs in philosophy. In recent years, our M.A. students have been admitted with multi-year funding packages to Ph.D. programs at Brown University, Columbia University, Cornell University, the University of Michigan, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Princeton University, the University of Southern California, Stanford University, the University of Texas at Austin, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, among many others. The M.A. program draws on the same faculty and graduate seminars as our Ph.D. program, and M.A. students are integrated into the regular life of the department.
Program name: Master of Arts in Philosophy

description: The graduate program in philosophy at UC San-Diego is a Ph.D. program. The department offers a broad range of courses, a distinguished and dedicated faculty, a diverse and excellent group of graduate students, and a supportive intellectual environment in which to pursue graduate work. The program is designed to be completed in five years. The curriculum is flexible, designed to allow students to develop their own interests, while at the same time insuring that they receive a solid grounding in the core areas of philosophy.
Program name: PhD in Philosophy

description: The Department of Physics offers a terminal M.S. program for students wishing to obtain a master's degree before pursuing a career in industry, business, education, or government. The program consists of a minimum of 36 units, which must include at least 24 units of graduate-level physics coursework. The program is designed to be completed in one to two academic years. The M.S. is a Plan II (comprehensive exam) degree. The comprehensive exam consists of the General Physics Exam, which is offered once a year at the start of the fall quarter. Incoming M.S. students have two opportunities to pass the General Physics Exam. Required Courses: Must pass five courses, each with a grade of B- or better from: PHYS 200A, PHYS 200B, PHYS 201, PHYS 210A, PHYS 212A. Elective Courses: Must pass at least three elective graduate courses in physics, each with a grade of B- or better.
Program name: Master of Science in Physics

description: The UC San Diego Department of Physics offers a comprehensive Ph.D. program that prepares students for careers in academia, industry and national laboratories. In the first one to two years, students take core graduate courses and specialized courses in their chosen sub-discipline. At the same time, students are encouraged to get involved in research within the first year by participating in research projects with our faculty. After passing a qualifying exam based on core graduate course material, students focus on their Ph.D. research. All of our Ph.D. students are supported as teaching assistants or research assistants during their graduate career. The Ph.D. degree is granted in recognition of the candidate's demonstrated ability to carry out independent and original research in his or her chosen field.
Program name: PhD in Physics

description: The standalone M.A. Program offers a comprehensive, one-year course of study in Political Science. Students take ten courses, including courses in three of the four primary fields of the discipline (American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Theory). They write a significant research paper as their capstone experience. The program provides the intellectual and analytic tools for a professional career in public service, government, or the private sector. It can also serve as a foundation for further graduate study at the Ph.D. level.
Program name: Master of Arts in Political Science

description: The graduate program in Political Science at the University of California San Diego is a top-ranked program that provides doctoral students with the theoretical and methodological skills to conduct high-quality, cutting-edge research. The Department of Political Science offers the Ph.D. in four primary fields of study: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Theory. We also offer a secondary concentration in Methodology. Our students work closely with world-renowned faculty who are leading scholars in their fields. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in academia, research, and public service.
Program name: PhD in Political Science

Concentration name: Latin America, Southeast Asia, Northeast Asia, and China
description: The joint Ph.D. in Political Science and International Affairs is a collaboration between the Department of Political Science in the School of Social Sciences and the School of Global Policy and Strategy (GPS). It is designed to join the department’s expertise in political science research with GPS's regional and multidisciplinary expertise. Students in the joint program pursue a Ph.D. in political science with a special emphasis in international affairs. All students in the program take the political science courses required for a Ph.D. in political science. Students also complete a set of core courses at GPS in international relations, policy analysis, finance and management, and quantitative methods. Joint program students must have a regional concentration. Available regions are Latin America, Southeast Asia, Northeast Asia, and China. Students take at least four courses in their regional concentration area. The dissertation for a student in the joint program must be on a topic in international affairs.
Program name: PhD in Political Science and International Affairs

description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) is a professional degree that provides a population-based perspective and is designed to prepare students to investigate and manage public health problems. The MPH program provides grounding in the foundational public health knowledge, in addition to concentration-specific knowledge, that will enable them to apply public health principles to a variety of settings. Students learn about the social and behavioral sciences, epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, and health services administration as well as their application to public health problems. Through a combination of coursework, a hands-on applied practical experience, and a capstone project, students learn to apply public health principles to real-world problems. MPH graduates go on to careers in a wide range of fields in both the public and private sectors.
Accreditation status: The Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).
Program name: Master of Public Health (MPH)

Concentration name: Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Behavior, Public Mental Health
description:
The PhD in Public Health is an interdisciplinary program offered by the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science in partnership with San Diego State University’s (SDSU) School of Public Health. This unique doctoral program, also known as the Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Public Health, provides rigorous training for future leaders in public health. Students in the PhD program have the opportunity to specialize in one of four concentrations: Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Behavior, or Public Mental Health.

The program provides students with a strong academic foundation in the core disciplines of public health, in-depth training in one of the specialized areas of concentration, and the skills needed to conduct independent, interdisciplinary research. Graduates from this program are prepared for leadership roles in academic institutions, public health agencies at the local, state, federal, and international levels, and in the private sector.
Accreditation status: The Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH). CEPH is an independent agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education to accredit schools of public health and public health programs outside schools of public health. Our initial accreditation term is for five years, extending through July 1, 2027.
Program name: PhD in Public Health

description: The M.S. in Sociology is a new graduate program at UCSD designed to provide students with a strong foundation in sociological theory, research methods, and a chosen substantive area of study. The M.S. degree is earned with the completion of 40 units of coursework, a major paper, and a comprehensive exam. It is a one-year program with courses that introduce students to the key ideas and debates in sociology and provide them with the skills to conduct their own research. Students will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty members who are leaders in their fields, and to develop their own research interests. The program is ideal for students who want to pursue a career in research, policy, or the non-profit sector, as well as for those who want to continue on to a Ph.D. program in sociology or a related field.
Program name: Master of Science in Sociology

Concentration name: Inequality and Social Stratification (race, class, gender, and sexuality)
description: The graduate program in Sociology at UCSD offers a PhD in Sociology. The program is designed to provide the theoretical background and methodological tools necessary for scholarly research and teaching. The faculty has a collective expertise in a broad range of sociological theory from classical to contemporary, and we offer rigorous training in both quantitative and qualitative methods. In addition to general theory and methods, the program provides specialized training in eight areas of specialization: Comparative-Historical Sociology; Inequality and Social Stratification; Political Sociology and Social Movements; Sociology of Culture; Sociology of Education; Sociology of Law; Sociology of Migration; and Science, Technology and Medicine.
Program name: PhD in Sociology

Concentration name: Structural Health Monitoring, Prognosis, and Validated Simulations (SHM)
description: The M.S. degree program is intended to provide students with the additional depth and breadth of knowledge, and training in research, for a successful career in the structural engineering profession. The M.S. degree can be a terminal degree or a prelude to a Ph.D. degree. The M.S. program has a thesis and a comprehensive examination option. Full-time students are expected to complete the degree requirements in one to two years.
Program name: Master of Science in Structural Engineering

Concentration name: Structural Health Monitoring and Nondestructive Evaluation (SHM-NDE)
description: The SE PhD is a research-oriented degree program with the objective of providing students with a broad background in one or more fundamental areas of structural engineering, as well as the ability to perform independent research. At the PhD level, the department offers a wide range of opportunities for advanced coursework and research with a focus on both traditional and emerging areas of structural engineering. The program of study is designed by the student and the adviser on an individual basis to meet the student’s research and career goals. Students admitted to the PhD program may be permitted to obtain the MS degree first, but an MS degree is not a prerequisite for the PhD degree.
Program name: PhD in Structural Engineering

description:
The MFA program in Visual Arts is a two-to-three-year, studio-based course of study for artists. The program is unique in that it encourages a diversity of art practices and allows for a wide range of explorations in a climate of critical exchange. The department promotes intensive inquiry, and students are encouraged to engage in a manner of working that is thoughtful, rigorous, and adventurous. Faculty and students have at their disposal first-rate facilities, and through a program of visiting artists and critics, students are consistently exposed to a wide variety of contemporary art practices and perspectives. The small size of the program, with an average of eight new students admitted each year, allows for an intimate environment, fostering a vibrant and supportive community among the students and faculty alike.
The MFA program is a two-year program (although up to three years of residency is permitted, with normative time being two years). It requires a total of 72 units for the degree. At least 50% of the course work must be at the graduate level in the department of Visual Arts. Course work is determined in consultation between the student and their faculty advisor. While the curriculum is highly individualized, students are required to complete a minimum number of credits in the following areas: Graduate Studio (VIS 201-209), Visual Arts Seminar (VIS 219), Art Practice Graduate Seminar (VIS 220), one course in art history/theory/criticism at either the graduate or upper-division undergraduate level, and the First & Final Year MFA Reviews (VIS 297 & VIS 298).
Program name: Master of Fine Arts in Visual Arts

description: The Ph.D. Program in Art History, Theory, and Criticism is a multi-faceted program that offers students a combination of carefully guided research and intellectual debate. Students follow a course of study that combines a broad education in the history and theory of art with a specific focus on an area of specialization. With a core of Art History faculty, and a large group of affiliated faculty, the program offers a wide range of fields of study. These include Ancient, Medieval, Renaissance, Early Modern and Modern European and American Art, Pre-Columbian and Latin American Art, and the Arts of China and Japan. In addition, students have the option to engage in interdisciplinary research on topics in art theory and criticism, and architectural history and theory, drawing on the expertise of faculty in the departments of History, Literature, Ethnic Studies, Anthropology, Communications and the School of Global Policy and Strategy. The Art Practice concentration provides an alternative to the traditional art history Ph.D. for a select group of students who, in addition to their scholarly work, are also practicing artists. The Art Practice concentration seeks to create a new generation of artists/scholars who are uniquely equipped to meet the challenges of art practice and education in the 21st century. The concentration combines the curriculum of the Ph.D. in Art History, Theory, and Criticism with the curriculum of the M.F.A. in Visual Arts. The concentration offers Ph.D. students the opportunity to complement their scholarly research with a strong studio component that includes graduate-level art-making seminars, and independent studies with the department’s renowned studio faculty. Students in the Art Practice concentration are expected to produce an ambitious body of artwork as their dissertation.
Program name: PhD in Visual Arts

description: The Certificate in Business Administration is a four-course program that provides students with the fundamental building blocks of a business education. The program is designed for working professionals, recent graduates and international students who are looking to advance their careers or pursue a graduate business degree. The program gives students an in-depth understanding of the core disciplines of business and the opportunity to focus their studies in a particular area of business. The program offers two tracks: General Business Administration and Technology Management. The program covers a variety of topics and prepares students to face the challenges of today's fast-paced, global marketplace.
Program name: Certificate in Business Administration

description: The Business Management Certificate is a part-time program for professionals who want to strengthen their knowledge of key business functions. This program is for individuals who do not have an undergraduate degree in business, but want to gain business skills to pursue an MBA or a management position. This certificate is also ideal for professionals seeking a career change and entrepreneurs who have a business idea and want to gain a deeper understanding of business fundamentals. In this certificate program, you will develop a fundamental understanding of business concepts and practices. You will learn about managerial accounting and finance, marketing principles and supply chain management. This program also fulfills many of the prerequisites needed to apply for the Rady School’s MBA programs.
Program name: Certificate in Business Management

description: The Digital Marketing certificate is a comprehensive program that provides you with tactical knowledge in various digital marketing disciplines. The curriculum focuses on SEO, content marketing, paid search, social media, conversion optimization, web analytics, mobile marketing, and email marketing. Whether you are a business owner looking to grow your business online, a traditional marketing professional looking to upskill, or a beginner looking to launch a new career in marketing, the Digital Marketing certificate is designed to provide you with a strong foundation to grow your business and your career. Upon completion of this certificate, you will be able to develop and implement a successful digital marketing strategy.
Accreditation status: UC San Diego Extended Studies is accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC).
Program name: Certificate in Digital Marketing

description: The Gordon Engineering Leadership Center offers a depth and breadth of leadership courses that allow our engineering students to develop the skills needed to become tomorrow's engineering leaders. The Bernard and Sophia Gordon Engineering Leadership Center is the first undergraduate engineering leadership center in the nation. It was established with the mission to educate and train effective engineering leaders who are capable of developing new products and services for the good of society. The Certificate in Leadership and Management will give students the opportunity to learn and practice the leadership and management skills required to be an effective engineering leader. The goal of this certificate is to develop students into future engineering leaders by providing them with the necessary skills to lead and manage engineering teams and projects. The certificate prepares students for their future leadership roles in the industry by exposing them to leadership frameworks, project management techniques, business and innovation principles, and team engineering best practices.
Program name: Certificate in Leadership and Management

description: The Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) in the Architecture-based Enterprise Systems Engineering (AESE) program, offered by the Jacobs School of Engineering in collaboration with the Rady School of Management, is a graduate degree program designed for working professionals. The MAS-AESE degree has an option of a specialization certificate in Project Management, which is a graduate-level certificate program designed to provide students with advanced education in the art and science of project management. The curriculum provides a primary emphasis on the systems engineering and business aspects of managing complex projects. The program will equip students with knowledge and skills to become future leaders in project management.
Program name: Certificate in Project Management

description: The Certificate in Energy Analytics (CEA) is designed to give our MS and PhD students a mastery of the modern computational, statistical, and optimization tools needed to address the complex energy challenges of the 21st century. It leverages and complements the core MS/PhD curriculum in MAE by providing training in state-of-the-art topics that are highly sought by employers in the energy and technology sectors.
Program name: Certificate in Energy Analytics Analysis

description: The Department of Political Science offers a Certificate in Quantitative Methods, which is open to all graduate students at UC San Diego. The certificate program gives students from a variety of disciplines rigorous training in statistics and formal modeling. In addition to a core curriculum of courses on statistical modeling, research design, and formal theory, the certificate offers students a choice of elective courses on such advanced topics as causal inference, Bayesian statistics, experimental design, spatial data analysis, computational modeling, and network analysis. Students complete the certificate with a two-course capstone research project. The certificate requires a minimum of nine courses (36 units). Course requirements for the Certificate are independent of graduate degree requirements. Courses taken to satisfy requirements for the Certificate may be applied toward graduate degree requirements, with the approval of the student's home department. All requirements for the Certificate must be completed prior to or at the same time as the student's graduate degree.
Program name: Certificate in Quantitative Methods

description: The Certificate in Spatial Analysis provides graduate students at UC San Diego with a specialized set of skills and a credential that will enable them to compete for jobs in the growing fields of spatial data analysis, geographic information systems, and data science. Spatial data analysis is an interdisciplinary field of research that offers a powerful set of methods and techniques for analyzing spatial patterns in data—whether for research or commercial use. These methods are relevant to a variety of disciplines, including urban planning, public health, environmental studies, political science, economics, sociology, and engineering. The certificate can be earned by students in any graduate program at UC San Diego. It is also available to individuals who are not enrolled in a UC San Diego graduate program through UC San Diego Extension’s Concurrent Registration process.
Program name: Certificate in Spatial Analysis

description: The Event Safety Certificate provides a comprehensive education in event safety and security, from initial risk assessment to emergency planning and crisis response. Developed by industry leaders, this program addresses the unique safety challenges of both indoor and outdoor events, including concerts, sporting events, festivals, and conventions. You will learn to identify potential hazards, develop effective safety plans, and manage on-site security operations. The curriculum emphasizes real-world scenarios and practical skills, preparing you to ensure the safety and well-being of attendees, staff, and performers. By the end of the program, you will be equipped to lead safety initiatives, comply with regulatory standards, and mitigate risks in any event environment.
Program name: Certificate in Event Safety

description: The Professional Safety and Health Officer certificate program is a unique program designed for individuals who want to start a career in the safety and health field or for those who have safety and health responsibilities and want to take their knowledge and skills to the next level. The program is taught by practicing safety and health professionals and it gives participants the opportunity to build a strong safety and health foundation with a focus on leadership and management skills. This program covers the technical, managerial and leadership skills needed to be an effective safety and health professional. This program covers a wide range of topics, including fundamentals of occupational safety and health, safety and health management systems, risk management, leadership, and communication.
Accreditation status: This program has been approved by the Board of Certified Safety Professionals for Continuance of Certification (COC) points.
Program name: Certificate in Professional Safety and Health Officer

description: Safety and health specialists play a crucial role in preventing harm to workers, property, the environment, and the general public. They are responsible for a wide range of duties, from developing and implementing safety programs to conducting inspections and audits. They also work to ensure that all applicable laws and regulations are followed. The Safety and Health Specialist certificate is designed for those who have a role in the safety and health function in their organization, are looking to enter the safety and health field, or those who want to expand their knowledge of the field. The program emphasizes management and leadership skills in addition to technical knowledge. Students in this program will learn the tools and techniques needed to be a successful safety and health specialist. They will also gain the skills and knowledge needed to meet the challenges of the profession. This program is ideal for those who are passionate about safety and want to make a difference in the lives of others.
Accreditation status: Our program has been reviewed by the Board of Certified Safety Professionals (BCSP) and determined to be an acceptable program for those wishing to achieve the Certified Safety Professional (CSP) designation. This certificate is approved for the Cal/OSHA Training requirement for the Construction Safety and Health specialist.
Program name: Certificate in Safety and Health Specialist

description: The Safety and Health Fundamentals Certificate Program is a unique program that provides a solid foundation in workplace safety and health. The program is ideal for those entering the safety profession, as well as experienced professionals looking to enhance their knowledge-base and skills. The curriculum provides both introductory and in-depth coverage of topics that are essential for today’s safety professionals. Courses are taught by experienced safety and health professionals who are experts in their respective fields. Required courses are part of the curriculum for the Professional Certificate in Occupational Safety and Health.
Program name: Certificate in Safety and Health Fundamentals
